facts.raw_span: A white woman in her early 40s presented with generalized pruritus of 10-years' duration
She had no other medical history
She had been treated with topical corticosteroids with no control of the symptoms
Physical examination revealed erythematous papules, some of them crusted, and some excoriations located over the trunk and upper extremities
some scales and fissures were seen on her lower lip, sparing the surrounding skin, as well as inner mouth and upper lip
Blood test results including antinuclear antibodies and complement, along with urine porphyrin analysis were normal

The biopsy results showed spongiosis and erosions in the epidermis and a nodular lymphocyte infiltrate in the upper and mid dermis with a peripheral mantle zone surrounding a central germinal center with cells that were CD20 positive and BCL-2 negative
Phototest with a solar simulator was carried out with the immediate reading negative for UV-B, UV-A, and visible light
erythema appeared in the area irradiated with UV-A 48 hours afterwards

concepts.why: The patient presented with generalized pruritus of 10-years' duration and had been treated with topical corticosteroids with no control of the symptoms.
The patient had erythematous papules and a skin biopsy showing a nodular lymphocyte infiltrate with a peripheral mantle zone surrounding a central germinal center.
The patient had a positive phototest result with erythema appearing 48 hours after UV-A irradiation.
The patient had generalized pruritus and erythematous papules, which are common features of atopic dermatitis.
The patient had erythematous papules and scales on the lower lip, which are consistent with lichen planus.
The patient had erythematous papules and a skin biopsy showing spongiosis and erosions, which are features of psoriasis.
The patient had erythematous papules and normal blood test results, which are consistent with dermatomyositis.
The patient had erythematous papules and scales on the lower lip, which are features of pityriasis rubra pilaris.

rationales.F01: Generalized pruritus is a key symptom of chronic pruritus
rationales.F03: Lack of response to topical corticosteroids suggests a more complex condition
rationales.F04: Erythematous papules and excoriations are common in several skin conditions
rationales.F05: Scales and fissures on the lower lip are characteristic of lichen planus
rationales.F07: Nodular lymphocyte infiltrate and CD20 positive cells are indicative of cutaneous T-cell lymphoma
rationales.F09: Delayed erythema after UV-A exposure is a hallmark of polymorphic light eruption

frontier_selector.rationale: Delayed erythema after UV-A exposure is a distinctive feature of Polymorphic Light Eruption, outweighing the chronic pruritus and other non-specific findings
